name: PHILLIPS 66 COMPANY
brief_text:
Three detectors fired for Phillips 66 Company. Benford's Law analysis found the leading digits of award amounts deviate significantly from expected natural frequencies, with digit 1 appearing 36.2 percent of the time versus the expected 30.1 percent. Modification growth on contract SPE60223D0471 expanded at a rate far exceeding peers in petroleum refining, with a growth ratio of 5,175 compared to the industry average of 82.9. Isolation Forest flagged the entity as a multivariate outlier, driven primarily by concentration of all awards within a single agency and unusually high modification frequency relative to award count.

The Benford test yielded a z-score of 15.9 sigma and a p-value of 4.6e-07 across 1,213 transactions totaling 1.22 billion dollars lifetime. The modification growth z-score reached 15.9 sigma. The Isolation Forest anomaly score was 0.73 on a 0-to-1 scale, with modification frequency at 46.5 percent of awards receiving changes.

These statistical signals warrant scrutiny but do not confirm fraud. Phillips 66 is a major petroleum refiner with legitimate, sustained DoD relationships spanning decades. The single-agency concentration reflects the reality that defense fuel supply is a specialized market. Benford deviations can arise from legitimate business practices such as contract vehicles with standardized pricing tiers. The extreme modification growth on one contract may reflect legitimate scope changes in a long-term supply relationship rather than cost manipulation.
